note: one entry per module the reference ships and this project does not, plus the parts that have no public source. Within a module both sides ship, a difference in template count is granularity — the reference splits a page into more partials — and is not evidence of anything; those are covered by the parity register instead.

capabilities.capability: The reference ships its own component namespace alongside the core module directories
capabilities.evidence: Hyva_Theme holds the reference's own primitives — modal, slider, loading states — plus the form validation, cookie, private-content and script-init helpers in its companion module. MageObsidian answers the same need with MageObsidian_* modules and Vue single-file components under module-storefront/src/view/frontend/web/components, so the absence of a Hyva_Theme directory here is a naming difference, not a missing capability. The individual primitives are compared one by one below.

capabilities.capability: The bundle product page and its option pickers
capabilities.ourPath: Magento_Catalog/templates/product/form/bundle.twig and the bundle partials below it
capabilities.evidence: the reference gives Magento_Bundle its own directory; here the bundle buy box lives inside Magento_Catalog. Covered by pdp-types.guest.spec.ts, which buys a bundle end to end.

capabilities.capability: The configurable product page and its variant selection
capabilities.evidence: same shape as bundle: the variant picker lives inside Magento_Catalog here. Covered by pdp-types.guest.spec.ts and the swatch assertions in catalog-listing.

capabilities.capability: The grouped product page
capabilities.evidence: covered by pdp-types.guest.spec.ts.

capabilities.capability: Colour and text swatches on the product page, the listing and the layered navigation
capabilities.evidence: the reference keeps seven swatch renderers under Magento_Swatches; here the same rendering is inlined where it is used. This is the clearest case of why module-level absence is not a gap: the capability is exercised by the suite on both the product page and the layered navigation.

capabilities.capability: Stock status on the product page
capabilities.evidence: a whole module here rather than one template, and it shows per-source availability the reference's single stock-status template does not.

capabilities.capability: Tax and fixed-product-tax presentation across listing, product, cart and order
capabilities.ourPath: Magento_Weee/templates/pricing/adjustment.phtml plus the price partials in Magento_Catalog
capabilities.evidence: covered by pricing.guest.spec.ts on all four surfaces, against a seeded product carrying a fixed product tax.

capabilities.capability: Gift message on the cart and at checkout
capabilities.evidence: covered by gift-downloads-vault.spec.ts.

capabilities.capability: Price and stock alerts from the product page
capabilities.evidence: covered by compare-alerts.guest.spec.ts, which subscribes and reaches the observable effect.

capabilities.capability: Following a shipment from the account
capabilities.evidence: the fixture seeds a trackable order and order-documents.spec.ts asserts the shipment tab renders.

capabilities.capability: The advanced search form and its results
capabilities.evidence: covered by catalog-search.guest.spec.ts.

capabilities.capability: Cancelling an order from the account
capabilities.evidence: covered by order-documents.spec.ts.

capabilities.capability: Rendering Page Builder content on a CMS page, block or product description
capabilities.evidence: the reference ships eleven Page Builder renderers; a text search of the whole theme and of all nineteen storefront modules finds no Page Builder anything. A store whose content team uses Page Builder has nothing to render it with here.

capabilities.capability: Rendering the reCAPTCHA challenge wherever the platform demands one
capabilities.evidence: eight templates in the reference, nothing here. It is the same hole the parity register already carries for the login form, widened: the reference covers contact, newsletter, review, send-to-friend and checkout as well.

capabilities.capability: Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager and gtag integration
capabilities.evidence: six templates across Magento_GoogleAnalytics, Magento_GoogleGtag and Magento_GoogleTagManager in the reference; nothing here. The only analytics string in the theme is the word inside a privacy policy CMS page.

capabilities.capability: The product-list widget a content editor drops into a CMS page or block
capabilities.evidence: the reference renders the widget; here a CMS page carrying one renders nothing. This was already a gap candidate from the parity sweep, and the comparison confirms it independently.

capabilities.capability: The storefront half of an administrator assisting a signed-in customer
capabilities.evidence: four templates across the two LoginAsCustomer directories in the reference; nothing here, although login_as_customer/general/enabled is on in this deployment, which is what the environment probe reports as a relaxed control.

capabilities.capability: Holding third-party scripts until the shopper interacts, with a declared bypass
capabilities.evidence: the reference's init-external-scripts and its user-interaction-bypass companion let a store keep tag managers and chat widgets out of the critical path; a search here finds no equivalent. This matters more than its size suggests: it is the mechanism that keeps a third-party script from undoing the performance budget.

capabilities.capability: A carousel or slider primitive the templates can reuse
capabilities.evidence: the reference ships elements/slider.phtml; there is no slider component here. Product galleries here use their own implementation, so the gap is the reusable primitive, not the gallery.

capabilities.capability: Payment gateway UI shipped with the theme
capabilities.evidence: the reference ships PayPal and Braintree templates so those gateways look native. MageObsidian does not, and this audit already records the gateway surface as blocked for want of credentials rather than missing: a gateway's own module supplies its UI, and adopting the reference's would mean adopting its licence.

capabilities.capability: A checkout built for the theme rather than the platform's own
capabilities.evidence: Hyvä Checkout is listed as a separate product with no public source in the hyva-themes organisation, so nothing about how it works can be derived here. What can be said is what the vendor says: it is sold as a distinct checkout. MageObsidian's own checkout is a Vue island over the native quote endpoints and is covered end to end by the suite, so this is a gap in the comparison's sense — the reference has a product here that this project does not — and not a missing capability on the storefront.

capabilities.capability: A component library a team copies from rather than writes
capabilities.evidence: listed as a commercial component library distributed to licence holders. No public source exists, so this entry carries only what the vendor states and none of the weight of the entries derived from code.

capabilities.capability: Point of sale
capabilities.evidence: a separate commercial product for in-store selling. It is outside what a storefront theme does, and outside what this project sets out to be.
